{{Quote|If we'd let the Starkiller super weapon clear its facility, it could have made the jump to hyperspace before we got another weapons lock on it. That would have&hellip;''"<br />"''Yes, yes, of course.''"<br />"''And if you had to make a similar choice, one that could again mean the destruction of millions or even billions, would you do as you did then?''"<br />"''Yes, sir. I stand by my decision and would do so again without hesitation. Peace and security in the galaxy must be my primary mission.|Supreme Chancellor Palpatine and Jedi Master Darrus Jeht, discussing Jeht's attempt to destroy the Starkiller|<ref name="Dark Hope">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/livingforce/lf20060119DarkHope|text=Dark Hope|int=Dark Hope}}</ref>}}
The '''''Shadowblade''''', code-named the '''Starkiller''', was a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] crafted during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

==Description==
{{Quote|The Shadowblade's cloaking field is weakest when it prepares its weapons! To lock onto us, it has to relax its jamming!|Jedi Master Darrus Jeht, while battling the Shadowblade in the Cularin system|<ref name="last stand" />}}
The ''Shadowblade'' was a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] that was armed with a [[hyper-point destablizer]]. Regarded as a [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]], the [[Starship/Legends|vessel]] was considered by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] to be capable of [[Death/Legends|killing]] hundreds of billions of people.<ref name="dark soul" /> The [[Warship/Legends|warship]] was sleek and angular in shape, with a black-[[Color/Legends|colored]] [[Steel/Legends|steel]] [[Hull/Legends|hull]], and the ship was powered by a number of [[Deflector shield/Legends|shielded]] [[Engine/Legends|thrusters]].<ref name="last stand" />

The vessel possessed a secondary armament of several dozen [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]] that were concealed behind steel panels on the hull. The cruiser was heavily shielded and it possessed an impressive [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking suite]] that generated a [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] blocking field around the vessel, though the sensor field weakened when the ship targeted its turbolasers while preparing to [[Space warfare/Legends|fire]]. The ''Shadowblade'' was also equipped with a [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] and was capable of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] travel.<ref name="last stand" />

==History==
{{Quote|The world is almost uninhabitable, my lord. The loss of the hyper-point destabilizer and its delivery vehicle has caused a thermal shift in the planet's atmosphere and tectonic instabilities that may yet tear Kromus apart. We are continuing to monitor the world as you instructed, but it is increasingly difficult to remain in orbit.|An agent of Supreme Chancellor Palpatine, on the effects of the bombardment of Kromus|<ref name="dark soul" />}}
The ''Shadowblade'' was developed by the Confederacy of Independent Systems during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a conflict between the Confederacy and the Galactic Republic. Codenamed the "Starkiller", construction of the vessel commenced on [[Kromus]], the fourth [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Kro'eval system]]<ref name="dark soul" /> in the [[Esuain sector/Legends|Esuain sector]],<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> where the superweapon was housed inside a large [[Hangar/Legends|docking bay]] in a [[Unidentified Kromus research station|six-winged research station]] situated at the centre of [[Unidentified Kromus city|Kromus' largest city]].<ref name="dark soul" />

By around [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="20 BBY">The ''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]'' states that the [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|''Living Force'']] campaign is set one year after the [[Invasion of Naboo]], an event that is dated to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. As the ''Living Force'' adventure ''[[Below the Belt: Philology|Philology]]'' [[Cularin's disappearance|moved]] the campaign forward ten [[Standard year/Legends|years]] to the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and the adventure ''[[Night Eyes: Night's Homecoming|Night's Homecoming]]'' established that by Year 4 of the campaign over a year had elapsed since the events of ''Philology'', ''[[Dark Soul]]'' can therefore be dated to circa [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]].</ref> the ''Shadowblade'' was nearing completion; the vessel's weaponry was operational and the ship was only a few [[Standard day/Legends|days]] from being ready to enter service and missing only a few sections of paneling. The Republic learned of the existence of the superweapon and a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] led by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Darrus Jeht/Legends|Darrus Jeht]] was dispatched to destroy the ''Shadowblade'' and the facility that housed it.<ref name="dark soul" /> [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], the leader of the Republic, sought to use the mission to manipulate Jeht into massacring the population of Kromus and to that end he had the sensors of Jeht's [[Flagship/Legends|command ship]] [[Maelstrom]] rigged to emit false signals regarding the status of the Shadowblade.<ref name="last stand" /> Informed by false reports from Republic [[Spy/Legends|spies]] that the Starkiller was being built inside a remote research facility far from Kromus' population centers, Jeht conceived to destroy the vessel via an [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|orbital bombardment]] of the construction site.<ref name="dark soul" />

On arrival in the [[Star system/Legends|system]], the Republic force approached Kromus and attacked a Confederate fleet that guarded the world. Darrus Jeht scanned the facility that housed the ''Shadowblade'' and on realizing that the intelligence that he had received was flawed and that the cruiser was being built within a major city, the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] revised his plan of attack and sought to take out the superweapon through a [[Ground warfare/Legends|ground operation]] to spare civilian casualties. However, the near-complete Shadowblade powered up and prepared to launch, to attempt to flee the world to safety. Concerned that the vessel was about to escape, Jeht ordered all of his surviving ships to open fire and destroy the research facility where the superweapon was being built.<ref name="dark soul" />

The Shadowblade evaded destruction in the resulting bombardment due to the Republic forces firing on the wrong target as a result of the rigging of the ''Maelstrom''{{'s}} sensors by Palpatine.<ref name="last stand" /> Darrus Jeht assumed the superweapon to have been destroyed and ordered his fleet to retreat from Kromus. The bombardment of the planet caused tectonic instabilities and a thermal shift in the atmosphere of the world that killed billions of people and went on to result in the loss of all life on the world. In the aftermath, some agents of Palpatine remained in the Kro'eval system to monitor the world's destruction and were ordered to report to Palpatine's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] their findings, which the Chancellor believed would be useful to another weapon project.<ref name="dark soul" />

Jeht was troubled by the billions of deaths that he had caused on Kromus and the ''Shadowblade'' featured in a [[Dream/Legends|dream]] that the Jedi Master had about the battle.<ref name="dark shadows">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/livingforce/lf20060216DarkShadows|text=Living Force: Dark Shadows|int=Living Force: Dark Shadows}}</ref> The ''Shadowblade'' eventually entered service<ref name="last stand" /> and in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], shortly prior to the conclusion of the Clone Wars,<ref name="19 BBY">''[[Living Force: Last Stand]]'' is set shortly after the declaration of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] but prior to the end of the Clone Wars, events that are dated to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] by ''The New Essential Chronology''. As such it can be established that the events of the short story take place in 19 BBY.</ref> the Separatist cruiser tracked down Jeht and the ''Maelstrom'', which was on a mission to attack the Confederate-held world [[Corlax 4]].<ref name="One Minute to Midnight">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/livingforce/lf20060302OneMinute|text=Living Force: One Minute to Midnight|int=Living Force: One Minute to Midnight}}</ref> The Maelstrom subsequently changed course for the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]]<ref name="last stand" /> in the [[Thaere sector/Legends|Thaere sector]]<ref name="EAOC" /> and the ''Shadowblade'' followed in pursuit.<ref name="last stand" />

The Separatist cruiser arrived on the edge of the Cularin system shortly after the Maelstrom, to find the Republic warship damaged from a brief [[Battle of Cularin/Legends|battle]] with the Republic ships ''[[Primal]]'' and [[Undaunted (Republic cruiser)|''Undaunted'']]. Ignoring the stricken ''Malestrom'', the ''Shadowblade'' instead headed towards the [[Cularin asteroid belt]], with its crew intending to attack [[Cularin/Legends|Cularin]], the system's primary planet. On Jeht's orders, the ''Maelstrom'' set out after the Separatist cruiser in an attempt to destroy it before it could make it to Cularin and the Republic warship opened fire on the ''Shadowblade'' with [[Torpedo/Legends|torpedos]].<ref name="last stand" />

The ''Shadowblade'' changed course to intercept the Republic vessel and opened fire with its turbolasers, inflicting further damage onto the weakened ''Maelstrom''. However, Darrus Jeht lured the cruiser into a trap and while the ''Shadowblade''{{'s}} cloaking shield was at it's weakest while the turblolasers were setting their targets, the ''Maelstrom'' caught hold of the cruiser with a [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]]. The [[Cularin's disappearance|previous activity]] of the [[Darkstaff]],<ref name="last stand" /> a powerful [[Sith artifact/Legends|Sith artifact]],<ref name="Recursion">{{LivingForce|Belted In: Recursion}}</ref> had left a number of [[Time/Legends|temporal]] rifts in the Cularin [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] [[Asteroid field/Legends|belt]] and the ''Maelstom'' dragged the stricken ''Shadowblade'' into one such temporal disturbance.<ref name="last stand" /> Both vessels then disappeared and were never seen again.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|274&ndash;275|Maelstrom}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Starkiller was created by [[August Hahn|August]] and [[Cynthia Hahn]] and first appeared in ''[[Dark Soul]]'', a short story supplement to the [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|''Living Force'']] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] campaign that was published on [[Wizards.com]] in [[2005]]. The vessel went on to make a further appearance in the final Living Force short story ''[[Living Force: Last Stand]]'' in [[2007]], which was also written by the Hahns and was the first source to identify the vessel as the ''Shadowblade''.

The superweapon's codename "Starkiller" is a reference to the earliest drafts of the script for [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], where it was the surname for a number of characters and was later used to derive the surnames of the [[Star Wars]] protagonists [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="TMoSw">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref>
